_meta.purpose: Real, verifiable judgments only. The legacy app shipped a fabricated PRECEDENTS_DB (invented case names, amounts and 'resolved in N days') - deleted in this migration. See git history of legacy/precedents.json and legacy/api/index.js if you must see it.
_meta.verification_standard: An entry is `verified: true` only if a maintainer opened the source URL and read the judgment (or a citing judgment) confirming title, court, year and citation. The 6 verified entries below were checked on indiankanoon.org on 2026-10-30.
_meta.display_rule: UI shows ONLY verified: true entries, labelled 'Similar published cases'. Never display a win probability. When a category has no verified entry, the UI shows an explicit 'coming soon' state.

Workplace / Labour.title: Vishaka and Others v. State of Rajasthan and Others
Workplace / Labour.holding: Sexual harassment at work violates the working woman's rights to equality and to life with dignity; until Parliament legislated, the Court's guidelines (and the constitution of a complaints committee) were binding on every employer.
Workplace / Labour.note: The POSH Act, 2013 later codified these guidelines; cite both.

Police / FIR.title: D.K. Basu, Asst. Commissioner of Police v. State of West Bengal
Police / FIR.holding: Laid down the mandatory safeguards in every arrest - visible identification of the officers, a memo of arrest attested by a witness and countersigned by the arrestee, and the arrestee's right to have someone informed of the custody.
Police / FIR.note: Non-compliance is itself actionable; quote it in a habeas-corpus or misconduct complaint.

Police / FIR.title: K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) and Another v. Union of India and Others
Police / FIR.court: Supreme Court of India (Nine-Judge Constitution Bench)
Police / FIR.holding: The right to privacy is a fundamental right protected by Article 21; any State intrusion into privacy must satisfy legality, a legitimate aim and proportionality.
Police / FIR.note: Re-confirm the exact SCC citation string on India Code or the SC report - the search snippet truncated it.

General.title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
General.court: Supreme Court of India (Thirteen-Judge Constitution Bench)
General.holding: Parliament's amending power cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution - the foundation of every challenge to arbitrary State action.
General.note: Rarely pleaded by a litigant in a small case; keep it in the app as context for 'your rights', not as a remedy.

General.title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
General.citation: Decided 24 March 2015; reported at (2015) 5 SCC 1 (confirm the SCC volume/page)
General.holding: Section 66A of the IT Act was struck down as unconstitutional; section 69A and section 79 were read down with procedural safeguards.
General.note: The answer to a police complaint that invokes only section 66A for an online post.

RTI.title: CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay and Others
RTI.holding: Examined whether a school board is a 'public authority' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act and the scope of 'information' - including material an authority holds in a fiduciary position.
RTI.note: Do NOT state as a rule that answer sheets are always denied or always disclosed - the position depends on the facts and later decisions. Read the judgment before advising.
